title: The 1780 French Machine That Turned Sand Into Edible Bread
hook: In 1780, a French inventor built a machine that turned desert sand into flour—and was arrested before he could feed the starving.
why_this_can_go_viral: The absurd yet dark premise of turning sand into bread during a famine triggers immediate curiosity and outrage.

title: The 4,000-Year-Old Minoan Device That Purified Poisoned Water
hook: Before modern filtration, the Minoans built a bronze vessel that could make any poisoned water drinkable—then the recipe died with them.
why_this_can_go_viral: Ancient survival tech that could have saved millions—lost forever—taps into fascination with forgotten knowledge.

title: The 1973 Ford Engine That Ran on Household Trash
hook: Ford tested an engine in 1973 that burned your garbage for fuel—then the patent vanished and the lead engineer died in a car crash.
why_this_can_go_viral: Conspiracy-friendly premise about a car that could solve pollution and fuel crisis being killed by corporate interests.

title: The 1890s Japanese Alloy That Glowed in Total Darkness

title: The 16th Century Ottoman Pump That Lifted Water 100 Meters

title: The 1948 US Army Chemical That Made Soldiers Invisible for 30 Seconds

title: The 3,000-Year-Old Viking Compass That Worked Underground

title: The 1970 French Oxygen Tent That Reversed Aging
